key_insight: A two-level machine-learning workflow can rapidly map free-energy stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions, revealing where stable phases exist and where they do not.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical composition guide for designing more stable Pb- and Sn-based perovskite solar absorbers, especially by highlighting the high-iodide region as the most promising for stability.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data were used to speed up structure relaxations.
Secondary ML models predicted energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
The approach computed free-energy landscapes while accounting for alloy disorder and FA molecular orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate phase stability across quaternary composition space for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, and the abstract reports narrower stable regions for the Sn-based system.
watch_item: Because the workflow depends on ML surrogates and complex alloy configurations, predictions should be validated carefully near composition boundaries and in untested structural regimes.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
